title: Connect your AI assistant
description: Use your chosen assistant to read selected asset details and related tasks. You approve access and manage sharing in My AssetsFlow.

sections.title: Before you connect
sections.body: Use an account that can manage sharing for the asset or household. Have your assistant account ready. Use only the public HTTPS MCP endpoint and connection instructions supplied by My AssetsFlow for your account. Do not substitute a development address or the app homepage. Provider account tiers, organization policies and remote MCP support vary.

sections.title: Enable asset sharing
sections.body: Open an existing asset, edit it, review “Share this asset with connected assistants” and save. Check the setting on every asset before authorizing an assistant. Sharing applies to all your connected assistants, including assets you enable later; it is not a separate selection per assistant. Related task titles and checklist text can contain personal information.

sections.title: Connect and authorize
sections.body: Add a remote MCP connection in your assistant using the endpoint supplied by My AssetsFlow. Choose the documented OAuth sign-in option. On the My AssetsFlow consent screen, check the assistant identity and requested read access before explicitly approving. Return to the assistant and review its discovered tools. Never paste an app password, access token or service key into chat. If connection details or authorization options are missing, stop and ask support.

sections.title: Ask about your records
sections.body: Select or enable the connector in a new conversation, then try these prompts. Answers depend on the recorded fields and tasks, not live inspections. Ask the assistant to identify missing information instead of guessing. Calendar and usage-based schedules may have unknown remaining values; recorded readings are not live telemetry.
examples: Which maintenance tasks are coming up?
Summarize the recorded details of my car.

sections.title: Change shared assets
sections.body: Return to an asset’s edit screen, change its assistant sharing setting and save. Removing sharing stops new connector reads of that asset and its related tasks. Enabling another asset makes it available to all connected assistants. Ask again in a new conversation to avoid relying on information from an older chat.

sections.title: Disconnect or renew access
sections.body: In Settings → External AI connections, find the assistant, choose Disconnect and confirm. Also remove or disconnect the connection in your assistant’s settings. Revocation stops future access but does not remove information already held by a provider. For an expired connection, start the connection again from the assistant and review consent again.

sections.title: Codex CLI
sections.body: Use an installed, authenticated Codex CLI with Streamable HTTP and OAuth support; organizational MCP restrictions may apply. Codex model access requires an eligible ChatGPT account or supported API billing, separately from My AssetsFlow authorization. OpenAI includes Codex across ChatGPT plans, including Free and Go, with plan-dependent limits. CLI access is separate from Codex Cloud availability.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.body: If connection settings are unavailable, check the exact web or CLI surface, account tier and administrator permissions. If authorization fails, check the supplied endpoint, use the same My AssetsFlow account, restart sign-in and ask support if it persists; do not bypass consent. If assets are missing, check sharing, active status, account and household permissions, then request a fresh list. If a connection expires, reconnect from the assistant. Disconnect revoked or unwanted entries in both services.

sections.title: What stays outside the connector
sections.body: The connector reads approved structured asset fields and related tasks. It does not provide document contents, private notes, location, serial numbers, insurance policy details or private care/payment records. Task titles and checklists may still include personal text; review them before sharing. Creating or changing assets and tasks, file imports and other writes are planned. Information sent to an assistant follows that provider’s policies, including any retention or training settings. Disconnecting cannot erase past conversations.
